overview: A Department of State list of papers for decimal file 894A.7965 records two March 1940 telegrams from Warner at Taihoku concerning the disappearance and subsequent discovery of a Japan Air Transport Company passenger aircraft named ENVOY. The plane disappeared between Giran and Taihoku, was later found completely demolished with everyone aboard killed, and carried no Americans; the second telegram also reported on the disposition of the passengers’ bodies.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning the disappearance and crash of the ENVOY
subfiles.about: An administrative file list describes two March 1940 telegrams from Warner concerning the disappearance and fatal crash of the Japan Air Transport Company passenger plane ENVOY.
subfiles.summary: The first listed telegram, Taihoku no. 97 of March 9, 1940, reported that the ENVOY had disappeared between Giran and Taihoku and stated that no Americans were aboard; it also referred to an enclosed copy of a telegram to the Consulate General at Tokyo. The second, Taihoku no. 98 of March 13, reported that the plane had been found completely demolished and that all aboard had died on impact. It also addressed the disposition of the passengers’ bodies.

interest: The page preserves a compact administrative synopsis of two telegrams that are not themselves reproduced in the supplied text, documenting how a missing-aircraft report developed into confirmation of a total-loss crash. It is useful for the history of civil aviation in Japanese-ruled Taiwan, for reconstructing State Department reporting networks between Taihoku and Tokyo, and for identifying the official concern with whether Americans were among the passengers and how victims’ remains were handled.
